test_title: PYST 44: SSC CPO - Quantitative Aptitude (Held on 9 Nov 2022 Shift 2)
subject: maths
question: If two tangents to a circle of radius 3 cm are inclined to each other at angle of 60°, then the length of each tangent is:
solution:
**Given:**

Two tangents to a circle of radius 3 cm are inclined to each other at angle of 60°

**Concept used:**

An external point's tangents to a circle are equal.

SSS congruency criterion

Tan 30° trignometric ratio = 1/√3

**Calculations:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7f96235eea3435c132300b1f21278d8243aa56a6de9776b43ef3a4629de76e9b.png] 

Let AP and CP be the tangents drawn to a circle

According to the question,

∠CPA = 60°

So, AP = CP

In triangle PAO and triangle PCO,

⇒ AP = CP

⇒ AO = CO = radius of circle

⇒ PO = PO = common side

Triangle PAO and triangle PCO are similar, by SSS criterion, 

At the point of contact the radius of a circle is perpendicular to the tangent

So, ∠PAO = ∠PCO = 90°

Since AO = CO = radius

⇒ ∠PAO = ∠PCO

⇒ ∠CPA = ∠OPA + ∠OPC

⇒ 2∠OPA = 60°

⇒ ∠OPA = 60°/2

⇒ ∠OPA = 30°

In triangle PAO,

PAO is a right triangle with A at right angle.

⇒ tan 30° = AO/PA

⇒ 1/√3 = 3/AP

⇒ AP = 3√3 cm

**∴ The length of each tangent is 3√3 cm.**
